markers.description: Part of speech (e.g., a., s. f., v. a.)
English usage/register label (e.g., vul. for vulgarly)
Vernacular usage/sense discriminator (italicized Greek in parentheses)
Subentry or bolded phrase within the main entry

rules: Headwords start a new entry with \lx (bolded in print), followed immediately by grammatical endings and \ps.
English usage notes (like 'vul.') should be tagged with \ue.
Multiple senses are not explicitly numbered in print but are divided by semicolons, POS changes, or parenthetical Greek discriminators; structure with \sn 1, \ge ..., \sn 2, \uv ..., \ge ...
Parenthetical Greek text that restricts or clarifies a sense (e.g., (ἰσχνὸς)) should be marked with \uv.
Bolded phrases and idioms within a block (e.g., τὸ ἀδύνατον) act as subentries; mark with \se followed by its own \ge.
Cross-references using 'see' are marked with \cf pointing to the target lemma.
